title: OAuth redirect uses _self and the callback returns to root '/', destroying the chat the user was in (state loss)
description: Every entry point into the per-user MCP OAuth flow navigates the top frame with window.open(authUrl, '_self', ...) (IntegrationsMenu:521, PersonalMCPConnections:127 and :139), which tears down the entire SPA. The backend callback then redirects to _base_url(request) — the app ROOT '/' — on success (mcp.py:317) and to '/?error=...' on failure (mcp.py:296,316), never back to the chat (/c/<id>) the user launched OAuth from. So a user who clicks Connect/Verify/enable-tool from inside an existing conversation is dumped onto a brand-new empty chat after authorizing, losing their in-progress chat view. The chat-input draft is keyed by chatId (Chat.svelte saveDraft -> `chat-input-<chatId>`), and the root '/' mount only restores the no-suffix `chat-input` key (Chat.svelte:3421-3450), so the per-chat draft (including selectedToolIds) is never re-applied on return.
evidence:
IntegrationsMenu.svelte:521  `window.open(authUrl, '_self', 'noopener');`
PersonalMCPConnections.svelte:127  `window.open(res.authorization_url, '_self', 'noopener');`
PersonalMCPConnections.svelte:139  `if (res?.authorization_url) window.open(res.authorization_url, '_self', 'noopener');`
mcp.py:317  `return RedirectResponse(url=_base_url(request))`
mcp.py:69  `return str(request.app.state.config.WEBUI_URL or request.base_url).rstrip("/")`
impact: Connecting Notion (or any per-user MCP) from within a chat throws the user out of that chat onto root, losing scroll position/draft/feature toggles for that conversation. It also creates the 'I authorized but the tool isn't on' confusion, because the returned-to chat is a different (new) chat than the one where tools were selected.
suggested_fix: Persist the originating chat id + tool-enable intent before redirect (e.g. sessionStorage 'mcp-oauth-return') and have the backend callback redirect back to that URL (pass a return_to/state through oauth/start and echo it on the callback redirect), or open the authorization_url in a popup window (window.open(authUrl, 'mcpoauth', 'popup')) and resume in the original tab via a postMessage/poll, so chat state is never destroyed.
verdict_reason: All cited code exists verbatim and the bug chain holds. (1) All three OAuth entry points navigate the top frame: IntegrationsMenu.svelte:521 `window.open(authUrl, '_self', 'noopener');` (inside the `if (!(tools[toolId]?.authenticated))` branch, reached from a chat's tool menu), PersonalMCPConnections.svelte:127 (verify) and :139 (connectOAuth) both `window.open(res.authorization_url, '_self', 'noopener')`. `_self` replaces the current document, tearing down the SPA — there is no popup/postMessage path (grep found no message listener). (2) `_start_oauth` (mcp.py:108-147) persists an `oauth` dict (resource_metadata, client_info, redirect_uri, state, code_verifier) with NO chat/return-URL context. (3) The callback redirects to root unconditionally: mcp.py:317 `return RedirectResponse(url=_base_url(request))` on success, mcp.py:296 `f\"{_base_url(request)}/?error=...\"` and :316 on failure; `_base_url` (mcp.py:69) = `WEBUI_URL or request.base_url` = app root, never `/c/<id>`. No client-side `/oauth/mcp/.../callback` route exists (only the backend oauth_router), so nothing re-routes back to the originating chat. (4) Draft loss is real: saveDraft (Chat.svelte:8757-8771) keys storage as `chat-input${chatId ? `-${chatId}` : ''}` and is called with `getDraftChatId()` (=getVisibleChatId, line 1597) inside a chat, i.e. `chat-input-<chatId>`. On the root mount, Chat.svelte:3421-3423 reads `chat-input${chatIdProp ? `-${chatIdProp}` : ''}` with `chatIdProp` empty, i.e. the no-suffix key, so the per-chat draft including selectedToolIds (line 3449-3451) is never re-applied. The in-chat toast at IntegrationsMenu:507-512 even acknowledges the resulting 'you must enable it again after authorizing' confusion. Bug is genuine.

title: startMCPConnectionOAuth call in IntegrationsMenu has no try/catch and a missing authorization_url navigates to '.../undefined'
description: On clicking a not-yet-authenticated tool, the code first shows a toast.info promising 'Opening sign-in', then awaits startMCPConnectionOAuth WITHOUT any try/catch (516). The backend oauth/start can raise HTTPException(400) (mcp.py:148-149 MCPOAuthError, e.g. discovery/registration failure) or fail on network — the rejection is uncaught, so the user gets the 'opening sign-in' toast but no navigation and no error is ever surfaced (silent failure after a promise). Additionally, if the response succeeds but has no authorization_url, authUrl stays undefined and `window.open(undefined, '_self', 'noopener')` navigates the top frame to a broken URL ('.../undefined'), destroying chat state with no recovery. Unlike PersonalMCPConnections (which wraps the call in try/catch and guards `if (res?.authorization_url)`), this entry point does neither.
impact: For a per-user Notion MCP whose oauth/start fails (e.g. PRM/AS discovery error, DCR rejected, transient network), the user sees a 'signing in' toast then nothing — no needs-reauth/error signal — or gets silently navigated to a dead '/undefined' page losing their chat. Hard-to-diagnose 'connect button does nothing'.
suggested_fix: Wrap the startMCPConnectionOAuth call in try/catch and surface err?.detail via toast.error; only call window.open when authUrl is a non-empty string, otherwise toast.error('Could not start sign-in'). Mirror the guarded pattern already used in PersonalMCPConnections.connectOAuth.
verdict_reason:
The quoted code exists verbatim. IntegrationsMenu.svelte:494 defines the click handler as `async (e) => { ... }` with NO try/catch around its body (lines 494-535). At line 516 it does `const res = await startMCPConnectionOAuth(localStorage.token, serverId)` unguarded. startMCPConnectionOAuth (src/lib/apis/mcp/index.ts:45-49) ends in `.then(handle)`, and handle (mcp/index.ts:8-11) does `if (!res.ok) throw await res.json().catch(() => ({ detail: res.statusText }))`. The backend route /mcp/connections/{id}/oauth/start (backend/open_webui/routers/mcp.py:229-236 -> _start_oauth) raises `HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=str(exc))` on MCPOAuthError (mcp.py:148-149, e.g. discover_from_challenge / register_client failure) plus other 400/404 paths. So on a discovery/DCR/network failure the await rejects, the handler body aborts AFTER the `toast.info('Opening sign-in...')` (lines 507-512) — no toast.error, no navigation, an unhandled rejection. This is exactly the silent-failure bug claimed, and the contrast with PersonalMCPConnections.svelte connectOAuth (lines 136-143: try/catch + `toast.error(err?.detail ?? \`${err}\`)` and `if (res?.authorization_url)` guard) is accurate — this entry point has neither guard.

HOWEVER the secondary sub-claim (success-but-no-authorization_url => window.open(undefined) navigates to '.../undefined' destroying chat state) is NOT supported by the code: on success the backend ALWAYS returns `{"status": True, "authorization_url": authorization_url}` (mcp.py:147), so res?.authorization_url is always a real string on the success path; on failure handle() throws so line 517 and the window.open at 521 are never reached. The non-user branch getOAuthClientAuthorizationUrl (configs:303-306) always returns a template string, never undefined. So the data-destroying '/undefined' navigation scenario is unreachable.

Net: the core 'missing try/catch -> silent OAuth-start failure, misleading toast, no error surfaced' bug is real and code-proven (notion_relevant: a per-user Notion MCP whose PRM/AS discovery or DCR fails hits exactly mcp.py:148-149). The data-loss '/undefined' framing is refuted, which is why I downgrade from high to medium: this is a confusing degraded-UX silent failure, not chat-state destruction.

title: OAuth failure surfacing shows only a raw error CLASS name / OAuth error code as a toast, and only on root '/' — no clear needs-reauth signal
description: The only place the OAuth callback's error is shown is the root page onMount, which toasts the raw `?error=` string. The backend puts either the upstream OAuth error code raw (mcp.py:296 forwards request.query_params.get('error'), e.g. Notion 'access_denied') or a python exception CLASS NAME (mcp.py:316 `error={type(exc).__name__}`, e.g. 'MCPOAuthError', 'ClientResponseError', 'KeyError') into the query. The frontend shows that verbatim with no mapping to a user-actionable 'reconnect / re-authorize' message. It also only fires on the root route — if the redirect ever lands anywhere else the error is swallowed entirely. There is no distinction for invalid_grant/expired-refresh (which is terminal and REQUIRES full re-auth) versus a transient failure.
impact: When a Notion connection fails or the user denies consent, they see a cryptic toast like 'MCPOAuthError' or 'access_denied' on a chat they didn't start, with no guidance to retry/reconnect. A token-exchange failure (e.g. invalid_grant from a rotated-away refresh token) is presented identically to any other error, so the user gets no 'this connection needs to be re-authorized' signal.
suggested_fix: Map known error codes/classes to friendly i18n messages ('Authorization was cancelled', 'This connection needs to be re-authorized — click Connect again'), pass a stable machine-readable error code (not type().__name__) from the backend, and surface it next to the affected connection (or via a connection-scoped needs_reauth flag from getMCPConnections) rather than a one-shot root toast.
verdict_reason: The cited code exists verbatim. src/routes/(app)/+page.svelte:8-12 does `if ($page.url.searchParams.get('error')) { toast.error($page.url.searchParams.get('error') || 'An unknown error occurred.'); }` — it shows the raw `?error=` query string with zero mapping. backend/open_webui/routers/mcp.py:316 returns `RedirectResponse(url=f"{_base_url(request)}/?error={type(exc).__name__}")` — only the exception CLASS NAME is put in the query, str(exc) is discarded; and mcp.py:294-296 forwards the upstream OAuth code raw: `RedirectResponse(url=f"{_base_url(request)}/?error={request.query_params.get('error')}")`. `_base_url` (mcp.py:69-70) returns the bare site root (`WEBUI_URL or request.base_url` stripped), so the callback always lands on `/`, whose only handler is (app)/+page.svelte. A grep across src/ for `invalid_grant`/`access_denied` and any error-code→message mapping returns nothing, so there is no user-actionable mapping and no reconnect/needs-reauth distinction. The MCPOAuthError raised in oauth.py:119 (`HTTP {status} ...`) on a token-exchange failure loses its message body at mcp.py:316 and surfaces to the user as the bare token `MCPOAuthError`, identically to any other failure, with no terminal-vs-transient signal. The only over-statement in the finding is "swallowed entirely if it lands elsewhere": the backend always redirects to root, so it does not in practice land on another route — but the core claim (cryptic raw class/code toast, no mapping, no needs-reauth signal) is fully code-proven. Note that auth/+page.svelte:166-168 has the same raw-toast pattern but for the separate login OAuth flow, not the MCP callback.

title: Verify-triggered OAuth in PersonalMCPConnections silently navigates away and never refreshes the connection list on failure
description: verify() (123) treats `res.auth_required && res.authorization_url` as 'needs OAuth' and immediately does a full-frame _self navigation (127), tearing down the Settings modal and SPA. Because the backend verify endpoint returns auth_required for any oauth_2.1 connection lacking tokens (mcp.py:280-281), clicking 'Verify' on an unauthenticated Notion connection does NOT verify — it silently bounces the user into the OAuth redirect with only the implicit navigation as feedback (no toast explaining what happened). On real verify failures the only feedback is toast.error(err?.detail ?? `${err}`); if detail is a non-string (FastAPI can return a list/dict for validation errors) this renders '[object Object]'. After returning from OAuth the Settings modal is closed, so the user never sees the now-updated authenticated state until they manually reopen Settings.
impact: For Notion (oauth_2.1, no token yet) 'Verify' is indistinguishable from 'Connect' but gives no explanation before yanking the user out of Settings; a verify error object renders as '[object Object]'. The user cannot tell whether verify passed, requires auth, or errored.
suggested_fix: Before redirecting on auth_required, show an explanatory toast ('Sign-in required — opening Notion authorization'); normalize error rendering (handle string|array|object detail like AddToolServerModal.extractErrorMessage); and use a popup (not _self) so the Settings list can reload and reflect authenticated=true on return.
verdict_reason: The quoted evidence exists verbatim at PersonalMCPConnections.svelte:123-134. verify() does `if (res?.auth_required && res?.authorization_url) { window.open(res.authorization_url, '_self', 'noopener'); return; }` (lines 126-128) — a full-frame _self navigation with NO toast/feedback before it. The backend confirms the premise: routers/mcp.py:280-281, `if connection.auth_type == "oauth_2.1" and not (connection.oauth or {}).get("tokens"): return {"status": True, "auth_required": True, **(await _start_oauth(...))}` — and _start_oauth returns `authorization_url` (mcp.py:147). So clicking "Verify" on an unauthenticated oauth_2.1 connection (e.g. Notion) does NOT verify; it silently bounces into OAuth, behaving identically to the adjacent "Connect" button (connectOAuth, lines 136-143, rendered at line 173) but giving no explanation. The "modal closed after return" sub-claim is also proven: the OAuth callback redirects to the bare app root `RedirectResponse(url=_base_url(request))` (mcp.py:317) with no settings deep-link/fragment, so the Settings modal is gone and the now-authenticated state is invisible until the user manually reopens Settings. Strongest corroboration: the repo's OWN IntegrationsMenu.svelte:501-512 documents this exact silent-_self-redirect-without-toast as a known trap ("Without this toast, the click silently redirects to OAuth... a common 'I enabled MCP but the model doesn't use it' trap") and adds a `toast.info(...)` before its identical `window.open(authUrl, '_self', 'noopener')` (line 521). verify() lacks that toast. The finding is real and code-proven.

title: mcpConnections / mcpConnectionsLoaded stores are declared but never wired — connection state is not shared/reactive across the app
description: Two stores intended to hold the per-user MCP connection list and its loaded flag are declared in the global store module but are never imported, set, subscribed to, or read anywhere in src/ (verified by repo-wide grep: the only matches are the declarations). PersonalMCPConnections instead keeps a private local `connections` array (PersonalMCPConnections.svelte:22) loaded on mount, and IntegrationsMenu re-derives MCP tools from the $_tools store. As a result there is no single source of truth for connection/authenticated state: after an OAuth round-trip nothing updates a shared store, so other surfaces (e.g. the IntegrationsMenu 'authenticated' lock overlay) only refresh when their own data source happens to reload, reinforcing the 'I authorized but it still shows locked' trap.
impact: Dead, misleading API; no reactive propagation of connection/authenticated status across the IntegrationsMenu, Settings, and chat surfaces, so post-OAuth state can stay stale until a manual reload of each surface.
suggested_fix: Either remove the unused stores, or actually back the per-user MCP UI with them: have getMCPConnections populate mcpConnections / set mcpConnectionsLoaded, and have IntegrationsMenu + PersonalMCPConnections read from the store so an OAuth return (or a focus-based reload) updates 'authenticated' everywhere at once.
verdict_reason: Verified all claims against the actual code. src/lib/stores/index.ts:199-200 contains exactly `export const mcpConnections: Writable<any[]> = writable([]);` and `export const mcpConnectionsLoaded = writable(false);`. A repo-wide grep `grep -rn "mcpConnections" src/` returns ONLY these two declaration lines — the symbols are never imported, set, subscribed to, or read anywhere else in src/. The supporting claims also hold: PersonalMCPConnections.svelte uses a private local `let connections: any[] = []` (line 22) loaded via `onMount(load)` (line 151) and imports `tools` (not mcpConnections) from the store; IntegrationsMenu.svelte imports `tools as _tools` (line 11), keeps its own local `let tools: Record<string, any> = {}` (line 65), and renders the authenticated lock overlay from `tools[toolId]?.authenticated` (lines 495, 537, 581) sourced from getTools() — never from mcpConnections. So these two exported stores are genuinely dead, unwired, and misleading: there is no shared reactive source of truth for MCP connection/authenticated state.

title: No client-side persistence of the tool-enable intent across the OAuth redirect (selection genuinely lost; mitigated only by a manual-retry toast)
description: When a user toggles an unauthenticated MCP tool, the code does NOT add it to selectedToolIds before redirecting; it only fires a toast telling the user they must enable it again after authorizing, then navigates away (e.preventDefault at 496 specifically prevents the enable). The intent (which tool the user wanted on, in which chat) is never written to sessionStorage/localStorage. Because the backend always returns to root '/', and the per-chat draft that does carry selectedToolIds is keyed by the original chatId (not restored on '/'), the selection is genuinely lost for any non-new chat. The toast is an honest workaround but leaves a real footgun: the user must remember the connection, reopen the menu, and re-toggle, on the correct chat.
impact: After authorizing Notion the user returns with the tool still off (and, per finding 1, often on a different chat), so the model never receives the Notion tools unless the user manually re-enables — the canonical 'I connected MCP but it doesn\'t use it' complaint.
suggested_fix: Before redirect, persist {connectionId/toolId, chatId} to sessionStorage; on the post-OAuth landing, read it back and (if authenticated now) auto-add the tool to selectedToolIds for that chat (or pass it through the OAuth state and have the callback redirect back to /c/<id>?enableTool=...), so the enable survives the round-trip.
verdict_reason:
The quoted evidence exists verbatim and the bug chain is fully code-proven.

1) IntegrationsMenu.svelte:494-535 — on toggling an unauthenticated tool, the handler runs `e.preventDefault()` (496) and goes into the redirect branch, which fires the toast ("you must enable it again after authorizing", 507-512) and then `window.open(authUrl, '_self', 'noopener')` (521) — navigating the current tab away. Crucially, the enable branch that would write `selectedToolIds = [...selectedToolIds, toolId]` (522-533) is the `else` branch and is NEVER reached for unauthenticated tools. So the intent is genuinely never recorded in component state.

2) No persistence of intent anywhere. A grep across src/lib for pendingTool/enableToolAfter/sessionStorage in this flow shows the redirect branch writes nothing — no sessionStorage/localStorage entry capturing which tool the user wanted on or in which chat. (The sessionStorage usages that exist are unrelated: chat-input drafts, selectedModels, stream cache.)

3) The per-chat draft that DOES carry selectedToolIds is keyed by chatId. saveDraft writes `chat-input${chatId ? '-'+chatId : ''}` (Chat.svelte:8757-8772) and restore reads `chat-input${chatIdProp ? '-'+chatIdProp : ''}` (1258-1296, 3421-3422). So that draft is only restored when you land back on the same chat URL.

4) The OAuth round-trip returns to root, carrying no chat/tool context. Backend mcp.py: redirect_uri is hardcoded `${base}/oauth/mcp/{connection.id}/callback` (117/307) with no chat or tool id; `state` is a random PKCE state (128), not a return URL; and the success callback returns `RedirectResponse(url=_base_url(request))` i.e. bare root '/' (317), error paths to '/?error=...' (296,316). The non-MCP branch (getOAuthClientAuthorizationUrl -> /oauth/clients/{id}/authorize, configs/index.ts:303-307) likewise threads no return state. The frontend oauthCallbackHandler (src/routes/auth/+page.svelte:104) is for user login providers (google/microsoft/github/oidc), not this MCP re-enable flow.

Net: after authorizing, the user returns to '/' (a new/blank chat, not necessarily the original chatId), the tool is still off, selectedToolIds was never updated, and no persisted intent re-applies the selection. The toast is an honest manual-retry workaround, exactly as the finder describes. Medium severity is fair: no crash/data loss, but it is the canonical 'I connected MCP but the model doesn't use it' footgun, and the fix (persist toolId+chatId before redirect and re-apply on return, or thread a return URL through the OAuth state) is well-scoped.

title: Concurrent refreshes are not serialized; rotated Notion refresh token reuse revokes the entire grant
description: resolve_personal_bearer_token() reads the oauth dict off the in-memory connection snapshot, checks expiry, then unconditionally calls refresh_token() and writes the new tokens back. There is no lock/semaphore anywhere (grep for Lock/Semaphore in connections.py and oauth.py returns nothing) and no re-read of the latest token from the DB before refreshing. The middleware attaches every personal MCP connection and connects clients in a loop (utils/middleware.py:2311-2337), and subagents/multiple concurrent tool calls each independently call build_personal_mcp_connect_kwargs -> resolve_personal_bearer_token. When two of these run for the same connection with an expired/near-expired access token, BOTH read the same refresh_token and both POST grant_type=refresh_token. Notion ROTATES the refresh token on every refresh and keeps at most ~2 valid with a short grace window; the second worker presents the now-rotated-away token and Notion REVOKES THE ENTIRE GRANT, killing the connection for the user.
impact: Connecting/using Notion under any concurrency (subagents, multiple enabled tools, parallel tool calls, multiple browser tabs/workers) intermittently revokes the Notion grant and force-logs-the-user-out of the Notion MCP. This is the single most likely cause of Notion connections silently dying after working initially.
suggested_fix: Serialize refresh per connection id (in-process asyncio.Lock keyed by connection id, and ideally a DB-level advisory lock / row SELECT ... FOR UPDATE for multi-worker). Inside the critical section, re-read the connection's oauth from the DB, re-check expiry (double-checked locking), refresh only if still stale, and persist the new refresh_token atomically before releasing. Never start a second refresh while one is in flight.
verdict_reason: The quoted code at backend/open_webui/utils/mcp/connections.py:100-127 exists verbatim. resolve_personal_bearer_token reads tokens off the in-memory connection.oauth snapshot, checks `expires_at > now+300`, and otherwise calls `await refresh_token(oauth, ...)` then last-writer-wins persists via update_oauth_by_id_and_user_id — with NO re-read of the latest token from the DB before refreshing. refresh_token (oauth.py:258-282) takes `refresh = tokens.get("refresh_token")` from that same in-memory dict and POSTs `grant_type=refresh_token` with it. grep for Lock/Semaphore/in_flight/inflight across utils/mcp/ and models/mcp.py returns nothing — there is no serialization anywhere on this path, and update_oauth_by_id_and_user_id (models/mcp.py:275-278 → 260-270) is a plain UPDATE with no version/optimistic-concurrency check. So two concurrent resolutions for the same expired connection both read the same refresh_token and both present it — exactly the rotating-token reuse scenario. The race is real and code-proven. One caveat that REFUTES part of the finder's reasoning (and lowers severity): the finder's headline trigger, subagent fan-out, does NOT apply to personal MCP. _resolve_subagent_tool_ids (subagent.py:227-267) only inherits ids via _is_inheritable_external_tool_id (subagent.py:202-206), which returns true ONLY for `server:`-prefixed ids, never for the `user:mcp:` personal-connection ids handled in connections.py. Parallel subagents therefore never re-resolve personal MCP tokens. The middleware loop (middleware.py:2310-2337) is also sequential within one request, so the bug needs CROSS-request concurrency. That path still genuinely exists: two concurrent top-level same-user requests (multiple browser tabs, queued/overlapping chat turns, or the routers/mcp.py:250 /tools and /verify endpoints that also call build_personal_mcp_connect_kwargs) can each independently hit resolve_personal_bearer_token for the same near-expired connection and double-POST the rotated refresh token. For Notion, which rotates refresh tokens and revokes the grant on stale reuse, that revokes the connection.

title: invalid_grant on refresh is not terminal — stale refresh token is retried forever, never cleared
description: refresh_token() (oauth.py:258-282) calls fetch_json(), which raises MCPOAuthError on any non-2xx (oauth.py:118-119). When Notion returns invalid_grant (terminal — token rotated away, grant revoked, or refresh expired past 30d-idle/180d-absolute), the exception propagates out of resolve_personal_bearer_token without ever clearing oauth['tokens'] or marking the connection unauthenticated. grep for invalid_grant / clearing tokens in the mcp utils and router returns nothing. The persisted (now-dead) refresh_token is left in place, so every subsequent connect re-reads it and re-POSTs it, which for a rotated/revoked token keeps re-triggering grant revocation and never recovers without manual disconnect.
impact: Once a Notion refresh token is invalidated (which #1 makes likely), the connection is permanently broken: the UI still shows authenticated=true (since oauth.tokens.access_token is still present, mcp.py:196), but every tool call fails, and the client keeps replaying a revoked token. The user has no signal to re-auth and re-auth isn't triggered automatically.
suggested_fix: Detect invalid_grant (parse the token error JSON, or treat 400/401 from the refresh endpoint as terminal): on terminal refresh failure, clear oauth['tokens'] (and persist) so authenticated flips to false and the verify/start flow re-prompts OAuth. Only retry on transient (5xx/network) errors.
verdict_reason:
The quoted evidence is accurate and the bug is code-proven. In connections.py:116-127, resolve_personal_bearer_token calls `refreshed = await refresh_token(oauth, ...)` with NO try/except. refresh_token (oauth.py:258-282) calls fetch_json, which raises MCPOAuthError on any non-2xx (oauth.py:118-119: `if response.status < 200 or response.status >= 300: raise MCPOAuthError(...)`). On a Notion `400 invalid_grant`, the exception propagates and lines 120-126 — which build the new tokens dict, set oauth["tokens"], and persist via MCPConnections.update_oauth_by_id_and_user_id — never run. The stale oauth["tokens"] (dead access_token + dead refresh_token) is left in the DB untouched.

No caller recovers from this. (1) routers/mcp.py: _list_specs (line 250) is wrapped at get_mcp_connection_tools (269-270) and verify_mcp_connection (284-285), which only re-raise as HTTPException — no token clearing. verify_mcp_connection line 280 only triggers re-auth (auth_required) when `not (connection.oauth or {}).get("tokens")`, i.e. tokens entirely absent; after a failed refresh the tokens key is still present, so that branch is skipped and it falls through to _list_specs which fails again. (2) middleware.py:2383-2410 catches the exception only to `mcp_failures.append(...)` and `continue` — no clearing, no re-auth. The ONLY token-clearing path is the explicit user disconnect endpoint (mcp.py:241, `update_oauth_by_id_and_user_id(..., {})`).

The misleading-UI claim also holds: mcp.py:196 computes `authenticated` solely from `tokens.access_token` presence, which is never cleared, so the UI keeps showing authenticated=true while every tool call fails. grep for invalid_grant or any tokens-pop in the mcp utils/router returns nothing. The exception class also doesn't distinguish invalid_grant from transient HTTP errors, so even a deliberate caller couldn't safely clear without parsing the message.

Severity high (not critical): requires the precondition of an actually-invalidated refresh token (rotation / 30d-idle / 180d-absolute / revocation), there is no data-loss or security impact, and manual disconnect+reconnect recovers it. But the integration is silently and permanently broken with a deceptive authenticated=true and no automatic re-auth, which is a genuine user-facing functional failure.

title: resource (RFC 8707) parameter is omitted from the refresh request
description: build_authorization_url (line 213) and exchange_code (line 247) both include resource when resource_metadata.resource is present. refresh_token() attempts the same but reads it from oauth['resource_metadata'].resource. That works for Notion ONLY because resource_metadata is persisted in _start_oauth. However the spec (and Notion guidance) require resource on authorize AND token AND refresh = the canonical server URI. The refresh path here is the one most likely to drift: if a future code path refreshes from an oauth dict that lacks resource_metadata (e.g. a migrated/partial record), no resource is sent and the re-issued token's audience is unbound. More concretely, the value used is whatever PRM was stored; if the root-fallback PRM was ever used (see finding 5) the resource is the wrong audience and is then propagated into refresh as well.
impact: For Notion the value is usually correct (resource_metadata is persisted), so this is lower severity, but the refresh-time resource is silently dependent on the same PRM that finding 5 can corrupt, and any oauth record missing resource_metadata refreshes without an audience-bound token.

title: Root-fallback PRM yields the wrong audience (resource=https://mcp.notion.com instead of .../mcp); used whenever the WWW-Authenticate probe is skipped or fails

title: Refresh failure / invalid_grant is not treated as terminal: tokens are never cleared, so a revoked refresh token is retried on every connect
description: resolve_personal_bearer_token has no error handling around refresh_token. fetch_json raises MCPOAuthError on any non-2xx (oauth.py:118-119), including invalid_grant. The exception propagates up and the connect attempt fails, but the stored oauth.tokens (including the now-dead refresh_token) are left intact. The next connect reads the same dead refresh_token and POSTs it again. Per Notion's live-verified behavior invalid_grant is TERMINAL and reusing a revoked refresh token can revoke the whole grant; repeatedly retrying it is exactly the wrong response — the spec says clear tokens and force re-auth.

connections.py:116-127  `refreshed = await refresh_token(
        oauth,
        allow_localhost=...,
    )
    tokens = {**tokens, **refreshed, "expires_at": token_expires_at(refreshed)}
    oauth["tokens"] = tokens
    await MCPConnections.update_oauth_by_id_and_user_id(...)` (no try/except; no clear-on-invalid_grant)
oauth.py:118-119  `if response.status < 200 or response.status >= 300:
    raise MCPOAuthError(f"HTTP {response.status} from {url}: {text[:300]}")`

title: OAuth callback identifies the connection by id only (no owner/session binding); state is the sole CSRF guard and is absent before any /oauth/start
description: mcp_oauth_callback is unauthenticated and looks up the connection with get_connection_by_id (the only id-only lookup in the codebase) — it never confirms the caller is the connection owner, relying entirely on the secret state. Two gaps: (1) the state comparison passes when both sides are None — if no /oauth/start has run for a connection, oauth.get('state') is absent, so a request with NO state param satisfies `request.query_params.get('state') != oauth.get('state')` (None==None). It then fails only because exchange_code needs a valid code_verifier (also absent), so it is not directly exploitable, but the state gate itself is a no-op in that window. (2) state is per-connection, not bound to the initiating user's session/cookie, so it is a connection-level CSRF token rather than a session-bound one; anyone who learns the (256-bit secret) state could complete the flow against the victim's connection, injecting the attacker's authorization code/tokens into the victim's connection.
evidence:
mcp.py:290  `connection = await MCPConnections.get_connection_by_id(connection_id, include_secrets=True)` (no user check)
mcp.py:298-299  `if request.query_params.get("state") != oauth.get("state"):\n    raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Invalid OAuth state")`
models/mcp.py:212-220 get_connection_by_id returns the row with NO user_id filter
impact: The callback's authorization rests solely on the secret state; there is no session binding tying the OAuth completion to the user who started it. The None==None window and the lack of session binding weaken CSRF protection on a flow that writes OAuth tokens into another user's connection row.
suggested_fix: Reject the callback when oauth.get('state') is falsy; require a non-empty state on both sides and compare with secrets.compare_digest; bind state to the initiating user's session (store user id / a session nonce alongside state and verify it on callback).

The router is mounted at main.py:1607 (`app.include_router(mcp.oauth_router, prefix="/oauth/mcp")`) and the only http middleware (main.py:1531-1542 check_url) merely sets `request.state.token`; it does not enforce auth, so the callback is genuinely unauthenticated. mcp.py:290 uses `get_connection_by_id(connection_id, include_secrets=True)`, which in models/mcp.py:212-220 does `db.get(MCPConnection, id)` with NO user_id filter — contrast get_connection_by_id_and_user_id (models/mcp.py:225-236) which checks `row.user_id != user_id`. The sole authz guard is mcp.py:298-299 (`if request.query_params.get("state") != oauth.get("state"): raise HTTPException(403)`).

Gap (1) None==None is real: a freshly created connection stores `oauth = encrypt_secret({})` (models/mcp.py:197), so `oauth.get("state")` is None; a callback with no `state` query param yields `None != None` == False, so the state gate passes. The finder honestly concedes it is not directly exploitable: mcp.py:301-302 still requires a `code`, and exchange_code (utils/mcp/oauth.py:231-244) sends `code_verifier=oauth.get("code_verifier")` == None, which a PKCE-enforcing token endpoint rejects. So the state gate is a no-op only in that window — accurate.

Gap (2) is real: /oauth/start (mcp.py:229-236) requires get_verified_user and ownership, and generates state via create_state() = _base64url(secrets.token_bytes(32)) (oauth.py:32-33, 256-bit), persisted on the connection row (mcp.py:138). grep for cookie/session in routers/mcp.py returns nothing — the state is NOT bound to the initiator's browser session; it is a per-connection token. title: Editing connection.url after OAuth does not clear tokens; access token bound (resource=) to the old MCP URI is sent to the new URL
description: update_mcp_connection lets the owner PATCH url while leaving oauth.tokens intact (only key/headers/env/oauth are encrypted-merged; url is updated in place and nothing clears tokens). resolve_personal_bearer_token then returns the existing access_token and build_personal_mcp_connect_kwargs sends Authorization: Bearer <token-for-old-resource> to the NEW url. Impact is bounded because it is the owner's own token and the owner chose the new URL (self-inflicted), but it breaks audience binding and can leak a still-valid Notion token to an unrelated endpoint the owner repoints to.
evidence:
mcp.py:215-218  `updated = form_data.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
    merged = MCPConnectionForm(**{**existing.model_dump(), **updated, "id": connection_id, ...})
    _validate_form(merged, user, request)
    connection = await MCPConnections.update_connection_by_id_and_user_id(connection_id, user.id, updated)` (no token clear when url changes)
connections.py:139-140,158  `if bearer_token:

title: Concurrent chats/subagents for the same connection each refresh independently with no per-connection lock, reusing the same rotated-away refresh token -> Notion revokes the entire grant
description: resolve_personal_bearer_token reads the oauth blob, checks expiry, and if expired calls refresh_token() then persists, with NO mutex/lock/serialization of any kind. The connection is re-read fresh from the DB on every get_tools call (middleware get_connection_by_id_and_user_id include_secrets=True at line 2317), and parallel subagents each independently re-enter process_chat_payload -> get_tools -> build_personal_mcp_connect_kwargs -> resolve_personal_bearer_token via asyncio.gather (subagent.py launch is gathered; middleware.py:1562 and :5863 gather parallelizable tool calls). A grep for Lock/Semaphore/mutex across backend/open_webui/utils/mcp/, routers/mcp.py and models/mcp.py returns nothing. So two concurrent runs both read the SAME refresh_token from the DB, both POST grant_type=refresh_token with it to mcp.notion.com, and both consume the same single-use rotating refresh token.
impact: Per the live-verified Notion behavior, refresh tokens ROTATE on every refresh and reusing a rotated-away refresh token beyond the short grace window makes Notion REVOKE THE ENTIRE GRANT. With OpenWebUI's parallel subagents (run via asyncio.gather, all sharing one user+connection), a user running 2+ parallel subagents whose access token is within 300s of expiry triggers simultaneous duplicate refreshes -> the connection dies and the user must re-auth. This is the single most likely way Notion MCP breaks under real agentic load.
suggested_fix: Serialize refresh per (user_id, connection_id): hold an asyncio.Lock (keyed in a process-wide dict) for the whole read-token / decide / refresh / persist critical section, and inside the lock re-read the persisted oauth blob first so a refresh that just completed in another task is observed instead of re-refreshing. For multi-worker deployments add a DB-level advisory lock (e.g. SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the mcp_connection row, or pg_advisory_xact_lock) so serialization holds across processes, not just within one event loop.

title: update_oauth_by_id_and_user_id is a blind full-blob read-modify-write with no row lock or compare-and-swap -> lost updates drop the newest rotated refresh_token
description: update_oauth_by_id_and_user_id delegates to update_connection_by_id_and_user_id, which encrypts the caller-supplied in-memory oauth dict and writes the ENTIRE blob via UPDATE ... SET oauth=<full blob>. There is no SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, no optimistic version/CAS check (grep for with_for_update/for_update/FOR UPDATE/isolation_level returns nothing in mcp.py or db.py). Two concurrent refreshes that both read the same starting blob will both write their own full blob; the last commit wins and silently discards the other writer's freshly-rotated refresh_token. The refresh_token that the database ends up storing may be the one that has already been retired by Notion.

Next refresh then sends an already-rotated-away token -> invalid_grant / full-grant revocation on Notion. Also wipes any concurrent edit to other oauth fields (client_info, resource_metadata).
suggested_fix: Do the read-modify-write under a row lock (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the connection row in the same transaction) or use an atomic JSON merge / optimistic-concurrency token (version column checked in the WHERE clause; retry on miss). At minimum, re-read the persisted oauth inside the same locked transaction before merging the rotated tokens so the write is based on current DB state, not a possibly-stale in-memory copy.

title: Refresh failure / invalid_grant is swallowed as a transient status event; tokens are never cleared and no needs-reauth signal is raised, so every subsequent chat silently fails

The spec and Notion ground truth require: invalid_grant is terminal -> clear tokens, force re-auth, do not retry.

title: Access token is pinned into static headers at connect time; no refresh-on-401 mid-session, so long subagent runs that cross the token lifetime fail

The MCP SDK's OAuthClientProvider/TokenStorage (imported at client.py:8) is NOT wired into the personal connect path, so there is no automatic refresh on a 401 received mid-session. A session that starts with, say, 200s of token life left (it passed the >expiry+300 check only because of timing, or the token aged in-session) will start returning 401 from Notion mid-run with no recovery, aborting tool calls that should have just refreshed. The 2025-06-18 spec explicitly requires refresh on mid-session 401.
